checked.found: Battle of Ankara, July 1402 (sources give 20 or 28 July); Timur won and captured Bayezid; sons fought the Ottoman Interregnum for roughly a decade
Bayezid II invited and resettled Jews expelled from Spain in 1492, especially in Salonica and Istanbul
Selim beat the Mamluks (Marj Dabiq 1516, Ridaniya Jan 1517) and took Cairo in January 1517; Ottoman rule extended to Mecca and Medina
29 August 1526; Suleiman's decisive victory, Hungarian royal army destroyed in about two hours, Louis II died, Hungary partitioned

Year 1699 (signed 26 January) and name are right, and Hungary and Transylvania passed to the Habsburgs (one source notes the Banat stayed Ottoman). The results call it the first treaty the Ottomans were forced to conclude on European terms; none supports 'their first major territorial loss'.

Year 1729 is right (press licensed 1727, first book 1729), and the Hungarian-born convert and Turkish dictionary claims hold. But earlier presses run by religious minorities existed in Ottoman lands, so 'First Ottoman Printed Book' is inaccurate; he was the first Muslim to print with movable Arabic type.
21 July 1774; Russia gained Azov, Kerch, Yenikale and Kinburn; Crimean Khanate declared independent
Auspicious Incident, June 1826; Mahmud II forcibly dissolved the Janissary corps in Istanbul, clearing the way for reform
Edict of Gulhane proclaimed 3 November 1839; promised security of life, honor and property to all subjects, launching the Tanzimat
Constitution adopted 23 December 1876, credited to Midhat Pasha; parliament opened 1877 and was suspended 14 February 1878
29 October 1914: Ottoman warships (Yavuz and Midilli) struck Russian Black Sea ports, starting Ottoman entry on Germany's side
Signed 30 October 1918 aboard HMS Agamemnon; Allies gained the right to occupy the straits forts and Istanbul was subsequently occupied
Assembly abolished the sultanate 1 November 1922; Mehmed VI left Istanbul aboard the British warship Malaya on 17 November 1922
